subject: Trading
title: The Hunt Brothers Silver Squeeze
description: A quick win: understand The Hunt Brothers Silver Squeeze.

hook.text: In 1980, the Hunt brothers cornered the silver market, driving prices from $6 to $50 an ounce. Then it imploded.

buildup.text: Nelson and William Hunt began buying silver in 1973, fearing inflation would destroy the dollar's value.

discovery.text: They accumulated a third of the world's private silver supply—over 100 million ounces—using immense leverage.

twist.text: Exchanges changed the rules mid-game, allowing only sell orders in silver. The Hunts couldn't buy more to hold prices.

climax.text: Silver crashed from $50 to $11 in two months. March 27, 1980—Silver Thursday—saw the Hunts lose over a billion dollars.

punchline.text: You can corner a market, but you can't corner the rules.

quiz.question: Why did the Hunt brothers' silver squeeze ultimately fail?
options: Exchanges changed rules to allow only liquidating trades, breaking their corner
